$comment: Every npm package `eslint.strict.mjs` imports, at the exact versions this repo
installs and tests. The set was a hidden contract: a consumer following the
README hit `Cannot find package 'typescript-eslint'`, installed it, hit the next
one, and after nine rounds discovered the set does not resolve at all.
It still does not resolve without `overrides` -- see `npmOverrides` below. That
is not a stale note: the config's unicorn floor (72) pulls `eslint >= 10.4`,
while `eslint-plugin-react@7.37.5`, the newest published release, peers
`eslint <= ^9.7`. npm refuses the tree outright. Copying the config and deleting
imports was the only path that worked, which is why consumers vendor.
`sarj-lint-configs init` writes the overrides block and prints the install
command. `packages/typescript` installs exactly this set, so CI proves it
resolves and that ESLint can load the config with it.

ceilings.eslint-plugin-react: 7.37.5 is the newest release; it peers `eslint <= ^9.7` AND calls the `context.getFilename()` removed in ESLint 10, so on the ESLint 10 this config requires it fails to install without `npmOverrides` and then throws on the first file linted. eslint.strict.mjs therefore skips its 18 rules on ESLint 10+; `tests/strict-config-runs.test.ts` fails when a release fixes this, so the workaround cannot outlive the bug.
ceilings.typescript: typescript-eslint@8 peers `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`, so TypeScript 7 is rejected.
